newsitem.title: UK: New sugar freight orders cited, fixtures sluggish.
newsitem.headline: New sugar freight orders cited, fixtures sluggish.

text.p: A number of new sugar freight orders emerged on the London market on Wednesday but shipbrokers said the new business was taking a long time to become firm. E D & F Man quoted for 16,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Colombo plus various options for 20/25 March.
Man also open for a prompt 11,500-tonne bulk cargo from Thailand to between one to three ports in Japan.
Shipbrokers said CSR was in the market for 22,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Japan for 1/10 April, with the rate expected to be in the region of $18.
CSR's earlier order for a parcel of 16,000 tonnes on the same route was expected to achieve a rate of around $19.50, they said.
Market sources said Fiji Sugar Marketing's recent inquiry to London was still open and would probably fetch a rate of around $27.
Firmer reported business included Cargill, said to have fixed two bulk sugar cargoes from north Latin American origins.
It was firm with 16/20,000 tonnes from Rio Haina to US Gulf/Atlantic for 15/20 March and also with 14,000 tonnes from Puerto Quetzal to Morocco, with options of Morocco, Egypt, Black Sea and Baltic.
In other news, authorities in the Philippines have ordered an extension of a sugar import ban from March to July to ensure that large warehouse stocks are exhausted.
Sugar shipments from north Brazil's key ports of Recife and Maceio since September are running at around 35 percent behind last year, according to port authority statistics.
Since the start of September 1996 to the end of February this year just over one million tonnes of sugar have been exported against 1.55 million tonnes in the same period the previous year.
